nodes.line: You are early. Or late. I have lost track.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. The Leichhardt North order has been two cartons light every week since the week of the show and the invoice says otherwise every time. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. There is no rush, but there is a Friday.

Two people have already said no. They admitted it, which I did not expect, so now there is $73 owing to Leichhardt North and it is not going to walk in here itself. I have rung the number on the letter four times. I'll see you right for it.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

npcs.name: Ewan, delivery driver at Leichhardt North

nodes.line: Been here since before it was like this. Go on.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. I do the Leichhardt North run at half six and there is a stretch of it where the van gets followed, which I have told nobody until now. Half the street knows and half the street is pretending not to. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

You are the first person to stop all morning. I have got a bucket of odd keys in the back of the van and the Leichhardt North shop is shut, and the number on the door rings out. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. Just do not come back empty-handed.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

npcs.name: Jelena, the kid on the register at Leichhardt North

nodes.line: Do not mind the mess. It is structural now.

Not being dramatic about this. Three of the Leichhardt North regulars have started coming in together and going out separately, and the till is $39 down on those days. Nobody else seems to have noticed, which is its own problem. I will know if you skipped a bit.

I am told you do odd jobs. Everything Leichhardt North sells comes off a floor at Lilyfield, and the woman who runs it will tell you things she will not put in writing. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
Well? I can read your face from here.

Two people have already said no. We found a twelfth, which means the Newtown club now owes the association $66 it had budgeted on not owing. I have rung the number on the letter four times. I'll see you right for it.
Sit. Talk. Then I will decide how I feel.
Fair enough. You know where I am.
Cash only and no, I am joking. What do you want.

You are the first person to stop all morning. Somebody walked off with the float from the Newtown canteen at about quarter to six during the last home game, and I have a fair idea which somebody. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. Just do not come back empty-handed.
You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

Not being dramatic about this. The sprinkler line under the Newtown outfield has been leaking since Thursdays and the wet patch has started to move. Nobody else seems to have noticed, which is its own problem. I will know if you skipped a bit.

I am told you do odd jobs. The bloke who allocates grounds for the whole association sits at St Peters, and Newtown has been at the bottom of his list for two seasons. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
Before you start: did anyone see you.
No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
Right. Talk while I do this.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. Somebody has been tipping fill into the creek behind Panania since the long weekend and it is narrowing the channel a metre at a time. My wife says I should let it go. My wife is wrong. There is no rush, but there is a Friday.

Two people have already said no. They have agreed to a clean-up at Panania, which is wonderful, except the grant is $110 short and closes on the long weekend. I have rung the number on the letter four times. I'll see you right for it.
Alright. I am listening properly this time.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. We had 10 sandbags in the Panania shed on the long weekend and this morning we have got the pallet they came on. Half the street knows and half the street is pretending not to. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

You are the first person to stop all morning. People keep driving the low crossing at Panania at just gone midnight with the water over the sign, and one of them is going to be the one. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. Just do not come back empty-handed.
Say it plain and I will pay you plain.

nodes.line: If you are here about the sign, the sign is wrong.

I am told you do odd jobs. Whatever is happening to Panania starts upstream at Revesby, and there are people up there who have been saying so for years. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
I had a feeling. Go on.
